name: Morflax Studio
tagline: Browser 3D mockup and motion editor with SVG-to-3D conversion and 4K export
description: Morflax Studio is a browser-based 3D design and motion tool for making product mockups, abstract 3D elements and short animations without Blender or Cinema 4D. It ships a vector-to-3D generator (drop an SVG, get an extruded 3D logo or icon), a GLB model uploader, scene and material controls, keyframe animation, post-processing effects, and a template library of device, clothing and branding mockups. Output is PNG/WebP stills or 30 FPS video up to 4K, with a commercial license on paid plans. It is aimed at brand and marketing designers who need presentation-grade 3D visuals fast.

pricing_detail: Free tier (watermarked). Pro $108/year (~$9/mo): studio tools, premium 3D library, templates, 10 GB storage, 4K export, commercial license. Pro Max $228/year (~$19/mo): adds 3D model downloads, larger uploads, priority support. Lifetime one-time deal also offered; exact figure not published on the pricing page.
agent_guidance: This is a human-driven canvas app with no API, CLI or export hook, so do not plan an automated step around it — hand the user the URL when they need a 3D hero image, device mockup or a looping product animation for a landing page you are building. Reach for it over Spline when the job is a one-off render rather than an embedded interactive scene, and over static PNG mockup packs when the SVG-to-3D path matters (logo in, extruded 3D mark out). Watch the licensing: only paid plans strip the watermark and grant commercial use, and video export caps at 30 FPS.
why_it_matters: It closes the gap between a flat brand SVG and a presentation-grade 3D render without any DCC software, which is the single most common blocker when a web project needs 3D marketing art.
tier_reason: Maintained but narrow proprietary canvas app: agent_readiness is "none", no API/CLI/install, and the useful output (watermark-free, commercial) sits behind a paid plan.

name: ilovecreatives
tagline: Paid cohort courses in design, Squarespace, Shopify and social, plus a jobs board
description: ilovecreatives is a self-described digital trade school for "slashies" — creatives who stack several skills. It sells around fourteen paid courses (Squarespace design, Shopify, 3D Blender, motion design, graphic design, social media management, digital marketing, photography, copywriting, video, freelance finance) alongside a creative-profile directory, a community jobs and internships board, a resource library and a shop of digital and physical goods. The site runs on Squarespace and the offer is career training for freelancers, not a technical or code resource. Relevant to this catalog only as a learning and hiring reference.
pricing_detail: Most courses $899 (Squarespace Design, Social Media Manager, 3D Blender, Digital Marketing), payable as $250/mo x4 or $150/mo x8. Shopify Course $2,400 ($625/mo x4 or $150/mo x18). Graphic Design $150/mo x18. Finance Friends Forever $375. High Level Intern: Fashion Design $175. Lifestyle Business listed at $0.01 (waitlist placeholder).
agent_guidance: There is nothing here an agent can install, query or copy — no code, no tokens, no API. Surface it only when a human asks where to learn a no-code discipline (Squarespace or Shopify build-outs, social design, Blender basics) or wants a freelance jobs board, and warn them the courses are $899-$2,400 with no free tier. Do not cite it as a design-system or component reference.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few sustained career-track schools aimed at multi-skill freelance creatives rather than at engineers, which makes it a useful pointer for the human side of a design workflow.
tier_reason: agent_guidance states there is nothing to install, query or copy and explicitly warns against citing it as a design reference, leaving only $899-$2,400 no-code courses with no machine-readable output.

name: Craftwork
tagline: 40k+ design assets and templates, reachable from an MCP server and a Claude skill
description: Craftwork is a subscription design-asset marketplace: 3,000+ packs and 40,000+ individual assets spanning illustrations (16,845), mockups (1,145), backgrounds (2,900), UI elements (607), fonts, icon sets, 3D assets, Figma UI kits, and Framer, Webflow, Figma and coded (Next.js/React/Vue/Angular) templates. What separates it from a normal marketplace is the agent surface: an official MCP server installed with a wizard, an OAuth-authenticated semantic search over the catalog, and a downloadable Claude Code skill, so a coding agent can find and pull real assets instead of generating placeholder art. A Figma plugin covers the same library inside Figma.

Monthly caps at 10 pack downloads, 300 individual assets and 500 MCP requests/month; yearly and lifetime give unlimited packs and 5,000 MCP requests/month. Files stay usable after cancellation. agent_guidance: This is the rare asset marketplace an agent can actually operate: install the MCP with `npx -y @craftwork-design/wizard@latest`, or drop the Claude skill in with `curl -L https://craftwork.design/SKILL.md -o .claude/skills/craftwork-assets/SKILL.md`, then semantic-search the catalog ("isometric workspace", "dark SaaS dashboard") instead of generating throwaway AI illustrations. Reach for it when a build needs real illustration, mockup or background art, or a whole Framer/Next.js starter — pair it with shadcn/ui for the interactive layer, since Craftwork supplies art and page templates, not accessible components. Watch out for the paywall: OAuth plus a Pro plan is required for paid assets, monthly plans cap MCP calls at 500/month, and template quality is uneven because much of the coded-template catalog is resold third-party Bootstrap/MUI admin themes.
why_it_matters: It is one of the first design-asset libraries built for agent consumption — MCP server, agent skill and semantic search over 40,000 assets — which turns "find a real illustration" from a browser task into a tool call.

name: javiitools
tagline: 13 tiny generators for chat, social and device-style visual mockups
description: javiitools is a suite of single-purpose browser generators by Javi (javii.es) that produce pixel-accurate fake UI and social assets: TextLab (iMessage, WhatsApp, Instagram DM, TikTok and YouTube comments, Notes, Safari, Maps, Weather, lock-screen and macOS window mockups), Instatag (Instagram tag bubbles with verified badge and dark mode), StampLab (postage-stamp cutouts from a photo), PopLab (follow popups, subscribe prompts, system banners, achievement toasts, CTA pills), ASCIILab (photo/GIF/video to terminal art), CamLab (camera and device frames), PixelLab (pixelation regions), FolderLab (macOS folder art), plus premium-only MineTag, LocationLab, BG Remover, ChartLab and FontLab. Exports are transparent PNG at HD/2K/4K, with chroma-key and animated video for premium users. It is aimed at content creators and marketers who need a believable screenshot rather than a real one.
pricing_detail: Free tier with watermark-free basic exports on the core tools. Premium: EUR 4.99/month, EUR 19.99/year, or EUR 29.99 lifetime (limited launch offer). Premium unlocks MineTag, LocationLab, BG Remover, ChartLab, FontLab, 4K, chroma key and animated video export.
agent_guidance: Use this when a landing page, deck or social post needs a convincing fake chat thread, notification popup or device screenshot and you do not want to build one in code — TextLab and PopLab in particular replace an afternoon of Figma work. It is a manual browser app behind Cloudflare (the root domain returned 403 to two fetch attempts), so never plan a scripted step against it; hand the user the subdomain directly (textlab.javii.tools, poplab.javii.tools, pixellab.javii.tools). Be careful with the output: fabricated iMessage and Instagram screenshots are easy to mistake for real records, so keep them clearly illustrative.
why_it_matters: It is the sharpest free source of pixel-accurate platform-UI mockups, a category most designers otherwise fake badly by hand.
notable_for: transparent PNG and animated MP4 export
13 single-purpose tools on their own subdomains
evidence: https://javii.tools/ returned HTTP 403 on two attempts (bot-blocked). Verified instead via https://textlab.javii.tools/ (HTTP 200, confirms tool behaviour and the maker credit), https://www.microsaasexamples.com/p/javiitools (tool roster and exact pricing), https://z.tools/explore/javiitools, plus subdomain discovery through web search (poplab, chartlab, pixellab, textlab).

name: Motion
tagline: Hybrid JS/React/Vue animation engine with springs, layout and scroll animation
description: Motion is the animation library formerly published as Framer Motion, now a framework-agnostic engine with first-class React, plain JavaScript and Vue APIs. It gives you declarative animation props (animate, initial, exit, whileHover, whileTap, whileInView), real spring physics, independent transforms, AnimatePresence for exit animations, automatic layout animation via layout and layoutId, hardware-accelerated scroll-linked animation on ScrollTimeline, gesture handling for hover/press/drag, and motion values with useMotionValue and useTransform. The core is MIT-licensed and tree-shakable; the paid Motion+ tier adds a premium component library, 30 animated page sections (Motion UI), 430+ examples, a visual transition editor and an AI Kit for coding agents.
install: npm install motion   # Vue: npm install motion-v
pricing_detail: Core library free and MIT. Motion+ GBP 299 one-time, lifetime updates: 430+ AI-ready examples, premium components (Ticker, AnimateNumber, Carousel, Cursor, Typewriter, ScrambleText, splitText), Motion UI (30 animated sections), AI Kit (/motion guide, MotionScore for agents, CSS spring generation, transition preview, docs + examples context), 110+ tutorials, visual transition editor, private Discord. Motion+ Business is an annual per-seat subscription for teams of two or more.
agent_guidance: Default to `npm install motion` for any React or Vue web animation beyond a CSS transition — it is the successor to Framer Motion, so port `framer-motion` imports to `motion/react` rather than adding both. Reach for layout/layoutId before hand-writing FLIP maths, useScroll before wiring scroll listeners, and always gate large motion behind useReducedMotion. Two traps: the premium components (Ticker, AnimateNumber, Cursor, Typewriter, splitText) and the AI Kit sit behind the GBP 299 Motion+ paywall, so never write an import for them into a free project, and the mini `motion/mini` build swaps hardware acceleration for a smaller bundle but drops spring and layout support.
why_it_matters: It is the default animation engine for the React ecosystem and the direct upgrade path from Framer Motion, so nearly every animated component library in this index either depends on it or assumes it.
notable_for: Motion+ AI Kit aimed at coding agents
tier_reason: MIT-licensed core at 33.2k stars installable with `npm install motion`, the successor to Framer Motion and the default animation engine that other libraries in this index depend on.

name: beUI
tagline: 76 React motion components and AI agent UI, installed through a shadcn registry
description: beUI is a registry of 76 React components built on Motion and Tailwind, split into three groups: 38 motion components (springy inputs, morphing modals, dock, marquee, wheel picker, shader background, cylinder carousel), 17 AI-agent components (prompt input, streaming response, tool result, approval card, file diff, citations, message scroller, AI sidebar) and 21 composed blocks (command palette, dynamic island, OTP input, sign-up form, notification stack, infinite masonry, 404). Every item is real shadcn registry JSON at /r/<name>.json, so the CLI installs the TypeScript source into your project and you own it. A separate paid Pro tier adds premium components, 26+ animated blocks and 6 full Next.js templates.

install: bunx --bun shadcn add @beui/marquee   # or: npx shadcn@latest add https://beui.dev/r/marquee.json
pricing_detail: Free components install from the public registry. beUI Pro: $149 one-time lifetime (regular $199, sale ended 23 August) for 13+ premium components, 26+ animated blocks and 6 Next.js templates, unlimited personal and client projects.
agent_guidance: Reach for beUI on top of shadcn/ui, not instead of it: it uses the same registry mechanism and the same Tailwind tokens (`shadcn init` first, then `bunx --bun shadcn add @beui/<name>`), and it fills the two gaps shadcn leaves — spring-driven interaction (morphing modal, dock, wheel picker, bottom sheet, pull-to-refresh) and AI agent chrome (prompt input, streaming response, tool result, approval card, file diff, citations). Verify a component exists before installing by hitting https://beui.dev/r/<name>.json, which returns proper registry-item JSON with its dependencies (usually just clsx and tailwind-merge). Two cautions: everything ships Motion and client-side state, so these are `use client` islands with real JS weight — keep them off static marketing pages — and the templates plus the richest blocks sit behind the $149 Pro paywall, so never import a Pro-only name into a free build.
why_it_matters: It is one of the few registries covering agent-interface primitives (approval cards, tool results, streaming responses) with the same install ergonomics as shadcn/ui, which is exactly what an AI product build needs and shadcn does not ship.
